notes.title: Rate Reduction
notes.text:
Don, this was previously quoted with a $15,000 benefit maximum which was approved by underwriting.  My broker Elenz & Associates is competing against JR Katz (same broker that has Medline and didn't send the quote to us).  They have a quote from JP at .22%, and Standard at .24%.

My broker wants us to discount our quote to .22% or .23%.  I told him there is no way we can get that low.  I told him with a $15k max, we have no pricing flexibility.  He said he would be willing to try and sell RSL, with a $10k max, if we can get to .22% or .23%.

This is a new client for my broker, and he wrote over 20 lines of new coverage with me in 2002.

This will be a hard sell for the broker selling the lower benefit maximuum, if you could approve the pricing discount below.

Version #1 is the accurate plan design.

Manual .33% x .90 mrp = .297 x .90 u/w discount = .267 x .90 questionairre discount = .24 x .96 (Regional or additional mrp discount = .23%

notes.title: Rate Reduction Cont'd
notes.text: Don, I know this is a large discount, but this broker is asking for a favor to write this case.  Many of his cases in 2002, were sold at or above manual.  He does not make a habit out of making me discounti his cases.  The broker believes the LTD will allow him to write the medical and life coverage.  He will quote only RSL on the Life, if he is able to pick up this account.

notes.title: Revised Discounting
notes.text:
.23 is the lowest we will offer assuming the broker will accept a flat 10% commissions.  We will apply discounts as follows:  .335 x .85 (MRP) x .90 (quest) x .95 (UW) = .24 x .95 (reduction in comm) = .23   Don

Based on the lower comm, actual quest and 5% UW disc the manual rate is now .296.  When we apply 15% MRP (10% + 5% RMD) and an additional 5% UW the sold rate is .24.  Good luck
